description: n4096 B2 (11222us, single biggest shape) and n2048 B8: the CholeskyQR path uses an UNBATCHED per-matrix FP64 cholesky loop, and B200 FP64 is weak; with only 2-8 matrices the GPU is massively occupancy-starved (148 SMs idle). Restructure to a multi-CTA-per-matrix tensor-core blocked QR: split each large matrix across many CTAs so all 148 SMs are busy, do the O(n^3) trailing updates in BF16/TF32 batched GEMMs with FP32 accumulate, and reconstruct compact (H,tau) via the existing orhr_col-style path. Eliminate the FP64 loop.

FP32 Spotrf in place of FP64 Dpotrf for the n4096 B2 cholesky. REGRESSION: cuSOLVER's single-matrix Spotrf (SIMT, no tensor cores) is ~4.5x slower than the FP64 getrf_wo_pivot path on sm_100. s6 11208->50052us; geomean 1634->1856. Validates 22/22. Confirms a cuSOLVER library potrf precision swap is the wrong lever -- the win needs a CUSTOM tensor-core blocked cholesky (TF32/FP16 trailing Schur, the thing B200 is fast at); cuSOLVER potrf uses zero tensor cores at any precision.

Tensor-core mixed-precision blocked cholesky (g_chol_fp32=2): FP64 diagonal blocks (cuSOLVER Dpotrf on nb=512 sub-blocks, ~0.2% of FLOPs) + FP32 panel TRSM + SINGLE-TF32 trailing Schur GEMM G22-=L21 L21^T on tensor cores. REGRESSION s6 11208->66545us, geomean 1634->1898. Two issues separated: (1) single TF32 (eps~1e-3) at cond(G)~1e9 corrupts the factor (factor residual ~ cond(A)*eps ~ 1e1 >> gate 9.8e-3) so the colnorm gate fails and geqrf fallback runs ON TOP -> double work; (2) the blocked structure as written serializes per-block (FP64 promote/demote round-trips + full-block GEMMs writing both triangles). Next: 3xTF32 trailing (Kahan ~FP32) to pass the gate, then optimize the structure.

3xTF32 Kahan trailing for the tensor-core blocked cholesky. s6 STILL 67257us (geomean 1903). PROFILE (brief-2-trial-3-6f5f7b6e.nsys-txt) shows geqr2_gmem_domino (41.5%) + geqr2_smem_domino_fast (26%) DOMINATE = cuSOLVER GEQRF FALLBACK runs full QR; my chol's getrf_wo_pivot<double> diagonal blocks are only 5.2%. ROOT CAUSE (fundamental): CholeskyQR orthogonality error ~ cond(A)^2 * eps. At cond(A)~1e4-1e5 even FP32-accurate (3xTF32) cholesky gives colnorm_dev ~1e1-1e3 >> the 5e-2 colnorm gate -> gate fails -> geqrf fallback on top. This is WHY FP64 (eps~1e-16) is needed for single-pass CholeskyQR. Fix options: (a) bypass the colnorm gate and rely on the loose factor residual + tau-override; (b) CholeskyQR2 (second pass squares orthogonality error to (cond*eps)^2).

Bypass the colnorm gate for the B==2 tensor-core chol path. MILESTONE: s6 67257->14596us (geqrf fallback gone) and the FACTOR RESIDUAL PASSES (rc=0) -- the tensor-core blocked cholesky + orhr_col recon + tau-override is NUMERICALLY VALID without the colnorm gate (the gate was a false-positive at cond^2*eps). But s6 14596 > parent 11208 (geomean 1672 vs 1634): the blocked-cholesky structure is SLOWER than the FP64 getrf it replaced. Next: profile to find the bottleneck -- suspect (a) 16 serial per-block FP64 Dpotrf host launches, (b) trailing 3xTF32 GEMMs writing FULL blocks (2x FLOPs vs lower-only syrk), (c) FP32 SIMT Strsm panel solves.

nb sweep for the tensor-core blocked cholesky (3xTF32 trailing, colnorm gate bypassed). s6 vs nb: 256->15195, 512->14596, 1024->14000, 2048->13157us (monotonic). geomean 1658 at nb=2048 (best). PROFILE (trial-4, nb=512): the per-block FP64 Dpotrf (getrf_wo_pivot<double>) is 24.5%/6.75ms over 32 instances = ~3.4ms/rep = SAME as the parent's full FP64 potrf; my added FP32 SIMT panel Strsm (trsm_right_kernel) is 10.5%/2.9ms. FINDING: FP64-diagonal blocking ASYMPTOTES toward the parent as nb grows (nb=4096 = the parent's single potrf) and never beats it -- cuSOLVER's full FP64 potrf is the most efficient FP64 option; splitting only adds launch overhead + panel-solve cost. The win REQUIRES removing FP64 from the diagonal (CholeskyQR2 / shifted-CQR in FP32, cond(A)*eps_fp32~1e-3<=1 so 2 passes reach orth~eps). Still no improvement over parent 11208/1634.

Shifted-CholeskyQR3 (FP32, FP64-cholesky-FREE) for the n4096 B2 path. VALID (check pass, factor residual OK via tau-override) but s6 112225us (geomean 1988) = 10x SLOWER than parent. DIAGNOSED via in-path debug: single FP32 pass + CQR2 both fail -- cond(A)~1e4-1e5 means a TF32 Gram corrupts the small eigenvalues -> chol breakdown (NaN); an FP32-safe diagonal shift (2e-3*sigma_max) instead SWAMPS the small singular values -> Q1 colnorm_dev=0.75 (poorly orthonormalized) -> G2=Q1^TQ1 still breaks down at the last pivot (info2=[0,4096]). Robustness forces exact-FP32 Gram (SIMT GEMM, slow on B200) + a 3rd shifted pass. CONFIRMS: the FP32 CholeskyQR family CANNOT beat the single FP64 cuSOLVER potrf (3.4ms) at this conditioning -- every FP64-avoiding factorization either loses accuracy (cond^2 orthogonality wall) or costs more than the 3.4ms it saves.

FINAL state: mode-2 tensor-core blocked cholesky (FP64 diagonal nb=2048 + 3xTF32 trailing Schur, colnorm gate bypassed), CholeskyQR2/3 OFF. validate PASS, s6 13184us, geomean 1656.56 (regression vs parent 1634; the cleanest VALID tensor-core attempt left as HEAD with a profile). Also measured plain torch.geqrf on n4096 B2 = 52248us (4.7x SLOWER than the parent CholeskyQR path) -- the existing Gram+FP64-potrf+TRSM+orhr_col path is already 4.7x better than the cuSOLVER QR library. Profile brief-2-trial-7-d8ec2d11.nsys-rep.

7 trials on the n4096 B2 / n2048 B8 FP64-cholesky-elimination brief. PARENT geomean 1633.69 (s6 n4096=11208, s5 n2048=7152). NO trial beat the parent; best valid = trial 7 (mode-2 tensor-core blocked cholesky) geomean 1656.56. KEY CORRECTION to the brief premise: (a) the n4096 B2 FP64 'loop' is just 2 serial cusolverDnDpotrf calls whose getrf_wo_pivot<double> kernel is the path's #1 cost (30.6%/3.4ms); (b) n2048 B8 does NOT use cholesky at all -- it is the blocked-Householder FP16 path (_LARGE_HI), already swept exhaustively by prior briefs, so this brief's FP64 idea does not apply to it. MEASURED design space for the cholesky: T1 FP32 cuSOLVER Spotrf=50ms (4.5x slower, single-matrix Spotrf is SIMT-unoptimized on sm100); T2-5 FP64-diagonal tensor-core blocked cholesky (3xTF32 trailing, gate bypassed): VALID and numerically sound (the orhr_col recon+tau-override produce a passing factor from a non-orthonormal Q), but s6 ASYMPTOTES to the parent as nb grows (nb 256/512/1024/2048 -> 15195/14596/14000/13157us; nb=4096 IS the parent's single potrf) -- splitting the FP64 cholesky into blocks only ADDS launch+panel-solve overhead because cuSOLVER's full FP64 potrf is already the most efficient FP64 option; T6 shifted-CholeskyQR3 (FP32, FP64-FREE): VALID but 112ms (10x) -- cond(A)~1e4-1e5 means a TF32 Gram corrupts the small eigenvalues (chol NaN), an FP32-safe shift swamps them (Q1 colnorm_dev 0.75 -> pass-2 G2 breaks down at the last pivot), and the robust fix needs an exact-FP32 (SIMT, slow) Gram + 3 passes. Also: plain torch.geqrf on s6 = 52248us (4.7x slower than the parent) -- the existing INT8-Ozaki-Gram + FP64-potrf + tensor-core-TRSM + orhr_col-recon path is already 4.7x better than the cuSOLVER QR library. ROOT CAUSE: FP64 is REQUIRED for single-pass CholeskyQR orthogonality (error ~ cond(A)^2*eps; FP64 eps~1e-16 -> ~1e-8 < gate; FP32/TF32 -> >>gate), and cuSOLVER's full FP64 potrf is already optimal. OPEN DIRECTIONS I did NOT reach (the manager should weigh these): (1) THE BRIEF'S LITERAL PRIMARY ASK -- a multi-CTA-PER-MATRIX blocked HOUSEHOLDER QR on A directly (NOT cholesky). Householder is UNCONDITIONALLY STABLE so it sidesteps the entire cond^2 wall that killed every cholesky variant; the existing blocked_qr_2level kernels are 1-CTA/matrix (occupancy-starved at B=2, which is why CholeskyQR was chosen), and splitting ONE matrix's panel+trailing across many CTAs (cooperative-groups grid sync, or a left-looking panel + cuBLAS-batched compact-WY trailing that fills the device) is a major kernel rewrite I did not build -- this is the genuinely-unexplored structural lever. (2) The RECON (panel_solve_fused 18.8% + diag_lu_warp 12.3% = ~31%/3.5ms, the orhr_col reconstruction) is now CO-EQUAL with the FP64 cholesky as the s6 bottleneck and is mostly FP32/FP16 already, but a multi-CTA recon or a recon that avoids the per-panel LU could be a bigger win than the cholesky -- worth a dedicated brief. (3) Mixed FP64-diagonal + a SINGLE CholeskyQR2-style cleanup pass (keep pass-1 FP64 for a well-conditioned Q1, then one cheap TF32 pass) -- I tested all-FP32 CQR but not FP64-pass1 + TF32-pass2. (4) The n2048 B8 occupancy lever is a separate idea from FP64-elimination and needs its own brief targeting the blocked-Householder panel.

DIRECT blocked Householder QR for n4096 B2 (brief's primary ask): cuSOLVER tall-skinny panel geqrf + custom larft + cuBLAS TF32 compact-WY trailing (C-=V(T^T(V^TC))), native compact (H,tau) -- NO Gram, NO FP64 cholesky, NO orhr_col recon. CORRECT (check pass) -- the structure produces a VALID (H,tau). But s6 2706415us (~240x slower): the custom hh_larft_kernel is O(nb^2*m) in ONE CTA (its z[i] dot loops all m_rest rows serially) = the dominant disaster, plus 64 panels x 2 matrices of serial cuSOLVER-geqrf + 3 GEMM launches. STRUCTURE VALIDATED; next: build larft from S=V^TV via ONE cuBLAS GEMM (not the O(nb^2 m) kernel), widen nb, and try BF16x9 trailing.

Blocked Householder QR: larft now ONE cuBLAS S=V^TV GEMM + tiny O(nb^2) T-build (was O(nb^2 m) in 1 CTA). s6 2706415->55198us (49x), geomean 1867. CORRECT. Still > parent 11208: bottlenecked by 64 sequential panels x 2 matrices (cuSOLVER tall-skinny geqrf + S/W/trailing GEMMs serial, no B=2 batching). Profiling next; levers: widen nb (fewer panels), batch the 2 matrices in the trailing GEMMs, BF16x9 trailing.

FINAL blocked-Householder state: nb=128, TF32 trailing. validate PASS, s6 54605us, geomean 1872. Swept: nb 64->55198 / 128->54534us (wash -- per-panel cuSOLVER geqrf cost grows with nb); trailing TF32 54534 vs BF16x9 59048us (BF16x9 confirmed WORKING + FP32-accurate on this cuBLAS 13 stack via CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_EMULATED_16BFX9, but slower here since the trailing is a small fraction). PROFILE (trial-9 + trial-10): the PANEL factorization (cuSOLVER geqr2_gmem_domino 45.6% + geqr2_smem_domino_fast 30%) = ~76% of s6 and is the occupancy-starved wall at B=2 (2 CTAs); my larft is now cheap (S=V^TV GEMM). NEITHER nb NOR trailing precision breaks the panel wall. The brief's primary structure is fully built and CORRECT; the one remaining lever is a CUSTOM multi-CTA/TSQR panel factorization (large kernel) -- the direct Householder QR cannot beat the parent's CholeskyQR (11208us) until the panel is device-filling.

10 trials. PARENT geomean 1633.69 (s6 n4096=11208). No trial beat the parent; best valid HH geomean 1872 (s6 54605). I BUILT THE BRIEF'S PRIMARY ASK: a direct right-looking blocked HOUSEHOLDER QR on A (trials 8-10) producing compact (H,tau) NATIVELY -- no Gram, no FP64 cholesky, no orhr_col recon, unconditionally stable. It is CORRECT (validate PASS, factor+orth gates pass). Structure: per nb-wide panel -> cuSOLVER tall-skinny geqrf + larft (S=V^TV via ONE cuBLAS GEMM + a tiny O(nb^2) T-kernel) + cuBLAS compact-WY trailing C-=V(T^T(V^TC)). Trial 8 (naive O(nb^2*m) larft in 1 CTA) = 2.7s; trial 9 (larft via cuBLAS S-GEMM) = 55198us (49x faster); trial 10 (nb=128) = 54605us. PROFILE (brief-2-trial-9/10 nsys): the PANEL FACTORIZATION is the wall -- cuSOLVER geqr2_gmem_domino 45.6% + geqr2_smem_domino_fast(2048/1024/512) 30% = ~76% of s6, occupancy-starved at B=2 (cuSOLVER's panel geqr2 is 1-2 CTAs for one tall panel). NEITHER nb (64 vs 128 = wash, per-panel cost grows with nb) NOR trailing precision (TF32 54534 vs BF16x9 59048 -- BF16x9 CONFIRMED WORKING + FP32-accurate via CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_EMULATED_16BFX9 on this cuBLAS-13 stack, but the trailing is only ~6% so it doesn't matter) moves the panel wall. The trailing GEMMs are already device-filling (cuBLAS); the bottleneck is purely the serial cuSOLVER panel. ALSO (earlier, trials 1-7): the Cholesky family is dead at this cond -- FP64-diagonal blocked tensor-core chol asymptotes to the parent (best 13157us), and FP32 CholeskyQR2/3 either breaks down or needs an exact-FP32 SIMT Gram + 3 passes (112ms); plain torch.geqrf = 52248us (4.7x slower than parent). THE ONE REMAINING LEVER (the genuinely-unexplored deep kernel): a CUSTOM MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX panel factorization that fills the 148 SMs for one tall (m=4096 x nb) panel -- either (a) cooperative-groups persistent kernel that splits each Householder column's m-reduction + application across CTAs with grid-sync, or (b) batched-TSQR (split the tall panel into row-tiles, factor all tiles + both matrices in ONE cusolverDnSgeqrfBatched call = device-filling, then hierarchically combine the R-factors). TSQR's challenge is reconstructing the flat geqrf-compatible (H,tau) from the tiled reflectors -- non-trivial but the standard solution. This is a large kernel that warrants its OWN dedicated brief; the HEAD (ff79a571, the working blocked-Householder) is the right base for it -- a follow-up swaps ONLY the panel and keeps the validated larft + WY trailing. SECONDARY openings: (1) the orhr_col recon (~31% of the CholeskyQR s6) as its own target if the manager keeps the Cholesky path; (2) n2048 B8 occupancy is a separate idea (it is the blocked-Householder FP16 path, already heavily swept) needing its own brief; (3) batch the 2 matrices' panel geqrf in the HH path (cusolverDnSgeqrfBatched, B=2) to halve launch overhead -- small, untried.

Cooperative-groups multi-CTA device-filling Householder panel (cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel; m_rest rows split across all 148 SMs; grid.sync per column; produces flat geqrf (V,tau) directly -- NO reconstruction). CORRECT (check pass). But s6 897715us (~16x SLOWER than the cuSOLVER-panel HH = 54605). Cause: per-column grid.sync (3-4 syncs/col x n cols x 2 matrices) PLUS the step-4 trailing-within-panel apply looping over remaining columns c with a SEPARATE __syncthreads block-reduction per c (O(nb) serial block-reduces per column = O(nb^2)/panel). cuSOLVER's geqr2_domino is well-optimized for the tall panel even at 1-2 CTA occupancy, so beating it needs a heavily-optimized cooperative panel (single batched reduction over ALL remaining-column dots per column, warp-shuffle reductions, far fewer grid.syncs) -- the sync FLOOR alone (~n syncs/matrix) is a real risk near the parent's 11ms total. Definitive: the naive cooperative panel is not competitive; cuSOLVER panel + tensor-core trailing (54605us) remains the best HH variant.

FINAL state: best blocked-Householder variant (cuSOLVER panel, nb=128, TF32 trailing; cooperative panel dormant+documented). validate PASS, s6 54563us, geomean 1867. Both the brief's primary structure (direct blocked Householder QR, native compact (H,tau), no Gram/chol/recon) AND the device-filling cooperative multi-CTA panel are now BUILT and MEASURED. Neither beats the parent CholeskyQR (11208us): the panel is a sequence of latency-bound GEMV-like rank-1 updates that cuSOLVER's geqr2_domino already does near-optimally even at 1-2 CTA occupancy; the cooperative reimplementation is sync/reduction-bound (16x slower).

12 trials, exhaustive. PARENT geomean 1633.69 (s6 n4096=11208). No trial beat the parent; the brief's idea regresses on measurement. I built ALL THREE structural directions to completion: (A) Cholesky family [trials 1-7]; (B) direct blocked HOUSEHOLDER QR [8-10,12]; (C) device-filling COOPERATIVE multi-CTA panel [11]. ===(B) THE BRIEF PRIMARY ASK, BUILT + CORRECT===: right-looking blocked Householder QR on A -> native compact (H,tau), NO Gram/chol/recon, unconditionally stable. cuSOLVER tall-skinny panel + larft (S=V^TV via 1 cuBLAS GEMM + tiny O(nb^2) T-kernel) + cuBLAS WY trailing. validate PASS. s6: naive larft 2.7s -> cuBLAS-S larft 55198us -> nb=128 54563us, geomean 1867. PROFILE: the PANEL is ~76% of s6 (cuSOLVER geqr2_gmem_domino 45.6% + geqr2_smem_domino 30%), occupancy-starved at B=2. nb (64 vs 128 = wash) and trailing precision (TF32 54534 vs BF16x9 59048; BF16x9 CONFIRMED WORKING + FP32-accurate via CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_EMULATED_16BFX9, but trailing is ~6% so irrelevant) do NOT move it. ===(C) DEVICE-FILLING PANEL, BUILT + CORRECT===: cooperative-groups multi-CTA Householder panel (cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel, m_rest rows split across all 148 SMs, grid.sync per column, flat geqrf (V,tau) directly). validate/check PASS. But s6 897715us = 16x SLOWER than the cuSOLVER-panel HH. ROOT CAUSE (definitive, measured on BOTH panel implementations): the Householder panel is a SEQUENCE OF LATENCY-BOUND GEMV-LIKE RANK-1 UPDATES (each column: m-reduction for the norm + rank-1 trailing-within-panel apply). cuSOLVER's geqr2_domino already does this about as well as possible even at 1-2 CTA occupancy; a cooperative reimplementation pays an ~n-grid.sync floor + reduction overhead that is far worse. The panel cannot be made meaningfully faster than cuSOLVER here, so the direct Householder QR (best 54563us) cannot beat the parent's CholeskyQR (11208us). ===(A) Cholesky family, DEAD at this cond===: FP64-diagonal tensor-core blocked chol asymptotes to the parent (13157us); FP32 CholeskyQR2/3 breaks down (cond(A)~1e4-1e5) or needs exact-FP32 SIMT Gram + 3 passes (112ms); plain torch.geqrf=52248us (4.7x slower). ===WHY THE BRIEF'S PREMISE DOESN'T PAY OFF===: the parent path (INT8-Gram + FP64-potrf + tensor-core-TRSM + orhr_col-recon = 11208us) is already 4.7x faster than the cuSOLVER QR library and near-optimal; the FP64 potrf (3.4ms) and recon (3.5ms) are each efficient, and the occupancy-starvation the brief names is intrinsic to the Householder panel / FP64 throughput, not fixable by blocking or a custom panel. ===REMAINING OPENINGS (the manager should weigh; I judge these lower-probability but did not fully reach)===: (1) a HEAVILY-optimized cooperative panel (single batched warp-shuffle reduction over ALL remaining-column dots per column, ~1 grid.sync/column instead of 3-4, persistent-CTA) -- might cut (C)'s 16x but faces the ~n-sync floor near the parent's 11ms total; (2) batched-TSQR panel (cusolverDnSgeqrfBatched over row-tiles x 2 matrices = device-filling) -- the reconstruction of flat geqrf (H,tau) from hierarchical reflectors is the unsolved crux; (3) the orhr_col RECON (~31% of the CholeskyQR s6, panel_solve_fused + diag_lu) as its OWN target -- co-equal bottleneck with the FP64 chol, a multi-CTA recon may be a bigger win; (4) batch the 2 matrices' panel geqrf (cusolverDnSgeqrfBatched, B=2) in the HH path to halve launch overhead -- small, untried; (5) n2048 B8 is the blocked-Householder FP16 path (already heavily swept), a separate brief. HEAD 872f9aaf = the best HH variant (cuSOLVER panel + tensor-core trailing), the right base for openings (1)/(2)/(4); the cooperative panel code is present-but-dormant (_HH_PANEL=0) for opening (1).
